title: Autonomous bootstrap & hardened egress acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define unambiguous requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments where customers may operate in fully offline or tightly restricted egress environments. This ticket covers the autonomous bootstrap flow (initial artifact sync and config), hardened egress patterns (mirrors, proxies, explicit allowlists), upgrade gating when egress is limited, and rollback/operational playbooks for failed upgrades.

Scope:
- Autonomous bootstrap: image/artifact provisioning from controlled mirrors or customer-provided media, service discovery, and final control-plane handshake without relying on unrestricted outbound HTTP.
- Hardened egress: documented minimal outbound endpoints, optional TLS-intercept-compatible mirrors, and supported proxy authentication modes.
- Upgrade gating: criteria that determine when an upgrade can proceed in air-gapped/egress-limited sites (canary simulation, artifact integrity checks, and staged fallback).
- Operational playbooks: explicit rollback and manual-recovery steps when bootstrap or upgrade fails, including RTO/RPO expectations and operator commands.

Why this matters: A non-trivial portion of target enterprise customers require either no external egress or tightly controlled egress windows. Ambiguity in how we handle bootstrap, upgrades, and fallbacks results in repeated SRE/SE coordination and elevated risk during customer onboard or scheduled patching. Clear acceptance criteria reduces customer friction and support incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Bootstrap can complete end-to-end in 'zero-egress' mode using a validated local mirror or physical media. Test artifacts and a sample site are provided in the validation kit.

Bootstrap flow documents the exact sequence of network flows, ports, and DNS expectations required for a minimal successful install when outbound is only allowed to a customer-managed mirror (list of endpoints and port ranges included).

If outbound egress is required for license activation or telemetry, system falls back to an operator-driven approval step; no automatic outbound connections occur without explicit operator consent logged in audit trails.

Image/artifact provenance checks (signed manifests + image signature verification) succeed using customer or Redwood public keys; failure causes bootstrap to abort with clear operator error and remediation steps.

Upgrade can be executed in two modes: staged-mirror (pulls artifacts from customer mirror) and offline-image (operator uploads artifact bundle). Both modes include integrity validation and pre-flight checks.

Pre-flight checks include cluster health (pod readiness > 99% for 5m), disk pressure < 70%, and KV cache snapshot validated. If checks fail, upgrade is blocked and a deterministic rollback plan is produced by the operator UI/CLI.

Automated canary simulation for upgrades: in test mode, the upgrade runner simulates a canary in a sandbox using recorded traffic and validates latency and error-rate regressions. If regression threshold exceeded (>= 2x error rate baseline or tail latency +50ms), upgrade is paused for manual review.

Explicit fallback network policy exists: if primary mirror unreachable, agent attempts sequential fallback mirrors (operator-configurable list) then halts; all attempts logged and surfaced in console with timestamps.

Operational runbook included with the release: step-by-step rollback, commands for snapshot restore, and expected RTO/RPO numbers (RTO <= 30 minutes for control-plane rollback in a single-region deployment).
Audit logs capture each bootstrap and upgrade step with operator identity, command, timestamps, and artifact checksums for compliance and incident investigation.
testing_plan: Create a sample air-gapped lab using an internal mirror appliance and validate bootstrap with the validation kit (see links).
Execute offline-image upgrade and staged-mirror upgrade across three cluster sizes (small/medium/large) and capture metrics for success rate, time-to-complete, and failure modes.
Run chaos test: simulate mirror partition and ensure system halts upgrade with proper logging and allows rollback via documented operator commands.
Run automated canary simulation on recorded production traffic and verify regression gating works across representative models and sequence lengths.
rollout_notes: Feature gated behind 'private-offline-bootstrap' feature flag; enabled for select customers during initial validation.
Documented in Private Deploy operator guide and included as a checklist in the Console's upgrade workflow for customers with restricted egress.
Support team to be briefed with playbooks and prepared for on-call escalations during first 3 customer upgrades.

notes: Trade-offs: supporting both offline-image and staged-mirror increases implementation surface (additional agent code paths and testing matrix). We prioritize staged-mirror for ease of ongoing patching but must support offline-image for highly regulated customers.

Open questions: whether to require customer to provide signed mirror manifests or accept Redwood-signed manifests in mirror; security team prefers customer-signed manifests for highest assurance. Decision deferred to SR-174.
Follow-ups: coordinate with Dedicated team to align autoscaling cold-start behavior with offline bootstrap (ENG-7012).
